slo_title: Apply steady-state concepts to solve thermal equilibrium problems.

mcq.q: What defines the "steady-state" condition in heat transfer?

options.A: The temperature is uniform throughout the rod
options.B: The temperature at the boundaries is zero
options.C: The temperature does not change with time

mcq.answer_text: The temperature does not change with time

mcq.q: The general one-dimensional time-dependent heat diffusion equation (without internal heat generation) is ________. A. $$ B. $$ C. $$ D. $$
A boundary condition of the form \(\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}(0, t) = 0\) represents _________.
The general solution to the steady-state 1D heat equation $\frac{d^2 u}{dx^2} = 0$ is ________. A. $$ B. $$ C. $$ D. $$
In the steady state, the one-dimensional heat equation without heat generation simplifies to ___________.

sq.q: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has ends at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=\begin{cases} x, & 0\leq x\leq l/2 \\ l-x, & l/2\leq x\leq l \end{cases}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)
\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{l} \left[ \int_0^{l/2} x \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx + \int_{l/2}^l (l-x) \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx \right].\)

sq.q: \(\text{A bar of length 10 cm has ends at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=3\sin\frac{\pi x}{5}+2\sin\frac{2\pi x}{5}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Solve heat equation with } u(0,t)=0, u(10,t)=0, u(x,0)=3\sin(\pi x/5)+2\sin(2\pi x/5).\)
\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{10} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/100}.\)
\(\text{Note: } \pi x/5 = 2\pi x/10, \ 2\pi x/5 = 4\pi x/10. \text{ So } B_2=3, B_4=2, \text{ other } B_n=0.\)
\(\text{Hence } u(x,t)=3\sin\frac{2\pi x}{10} e^{-\alpha^2 4\pi^2 t/100} + 2\sin\frac{4\pi x}{10} e^{-\alpha^2 16\pi^2 t/100}.\)

lq.q: \(\text{A rod of length 10 cm has its ends kept at $0^\circ$ C and $100^\circ$ C until steady state.}\\ \text{Then the temperature at the far end ($100^\circ$ C) is suddenly reduced to $0^\circ$ C while the near end is maintained at $0^\circ$ C.}\\ \text{Find the temperature $u(x,t).$}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Steady state initially: \(u_s(x) = 10x\) (since \((100/10)x\)).}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{After change: BCs: \(u(0,t)=0\), \(u(10,t)=0.\) Initial: \(u(x,0)=10x.\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{General solution: \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / 100}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{\(B_n = \dfrac{2}{10} \int_0^{10} 10x \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) dx = 2 \int_0^{10} x \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Compute: \(= 2 \left[ \dfrac{-10x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right)}{n\pi} + \dfrac{100}{n^2\pi^2} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) \right]_0^{10}.\)}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Simplify: \(= 2 \left[ \dfrac{-100 \cos(n\pi)}{n\pi} + 0 - 0 \right] = -\dfrac{200}{n\pi} \cos(n\pi) = \dfrac{200}{n\pi} (-1)^{n+1}.\)}\) (3 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \dfrac{200}{\pi} \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{10}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / 100}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
